newsitem.title: USA: Minn. gov urges a full vote on Twins stadium plans.
newsitem.headline: Minn. gov urges a full vote on Twins stadium plans.

text.p: Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson on Tuesday urged lawmakers to give the full legislature an opportunity to vote on a financing package for a new stadium for the Minnesota Twins American League baseball team.
"Without legislative action on the stadium issue, I am convinced the Twins will depart Minnesota," Carlson said in a letter to lawmakers. "That would clearly be tragic."
The tax committees of both the House and Senate rejected financing proposals for a new retractable-roof stadium for the Twins on Monday.
Twins spokesman David St. Peter said Tuesday that the team would make no public comments on the stadium developments.

Twins officials have estimated the cost of a new facility at more than $400 million and financing proposals to pay for it have included cigarette tax hikes, special development districts and expanded gambling.
Carlson told legislators that the they had plenty of time to decide the issue in the last two sessions and an opportunity to put the stadium to a public referendum.
At minimum, legislators should have the opportunity to vote for a proposal directing a study of possible financing for a ballpark to be completed by the end of the summer, Carlson said.
"Let me be clear -- delaying the stadium issue places the future of the Minnesota Twins franchise in serious jeopardy," Carlson wrote.
House Majority Leader Ted Winter, D-Fulda, wants the planning and fiscal policy committee to study the stadium issue over the summer.
